title: The proposition leads on capability, not consequence
statement: The public proposition is organised around engineering capability, and states no commercial consequence of that capability.
implication: A hiring audience can tell what the subject does, and cannot tell what it is worth.
competitive_relevance: Both qualified comparisons make the same omission, so this is a shared weakness rather than a disadvantage.
audience_relevance: Directly relevant to the founder and CEO audience, who decide on consequence.

title: Transformation language is crowded; economics is not
statement: Both qualified comparisons lead on transformation language, and none addresses the cost consequences of technical decisions.
implication: A position built on economics would not compete for attention with the language the comparison set already occupies.

title: Seniority is claimed but not evidenced
statement: Seniority claims appear without quantified outcomes or third-party proof, which a hiring audience is likely to weigh heavily.
implication: The claim may be discounted by exactly the audience it is aimed at.
audience_relevance: Recruiters shortlist on evidence they can repeat to a client.

title: No third-party proof is published
statement: The site publishes no named client, case study or testimonial.
implication: Every claim on the site is self-asserted.
